html:
By tradition San Marino was founded on 3 September 301, when Marinus, a stonemason from the island of Rab in Dalmatia, built a small Christian community on Mount Titano, fleeing the persecution of the emperor Diocletian.

The story is a legend written down centuries later, but a community of monks and then a town grew on the mountain. Its people governed themselves through an assembly of family heads, and by the 1200s through Captains Regent.

San Marino claims to be the oldest surviving sovereign state and constitutional republic in the world. Its hilltop position and its poverty helped it survive the popes, the unification of Italy, which left it alone, and Napoleon, who offered it more land. 3 September is its national day. See San Marino.
